config.title: Build type guards for unknown API payloads

intro.title: Build type guards for unknown API payloads
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple function that validates data from an external API. You will learn how to create a type guard, which is a TypeScript function that checks if unknown data matches a specific shape or type. The main technologies involved are TypeScript's type predicates and object property checking. By the end, you'll be able to safely handle unpredictable API responses in your applications.
intro.usecase: When building applications that consume external APIs, you often receive data with uncertain structure that TypeScript can't validate at compile time. This happens in dashboards displaying third-party analytics, e-commerce platforms integrating payment gateways, or social media apps showing user-generated content. Type guards let you safely validate API responses before rendering data in UI components like charts, product listings, or user profiles, preventing runtime errors while maintaining type safety throughout your application.

objectives: Construct type guard functions to validate API response structures
Apply type predicates to narrow unknown types to specific interfaces
Implement runtime checks for required properties in dynamic data
Configure type guards to handle nested object structures
Integrate type guards with fetch operations to ensure type safety
Manipulate unknown data by applying successive validation layers
Initialize type-safe variables from validated API payloads

steps.title: Import TypeScript utilities for type checking
steps.instruction: Import the necessary TypeScript utilities that will be used for building type guards.
steps.hint: You'll need to import the 'unknown' type and 'is' type predicate utility from TypeScript.
steps.seedCode: // Import TypeScript utilities for type checking here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary TypeScript utilities are imported at the top of the file.
successCriteria: The 'unknown' type and 'is' type predicate utility are imported from TypeScript.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some utilities, but make sure to import both 'unknown' and 'is' from TypeScript.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import TypeScript utilities for type checking.

steps.title: Define the expected API response interface
steps.instruction: Create an interface named 'ApiResponse' that defines the expected structure of an API response. It should have a 'data' property of type string and a 'timestamp' property of type number.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define the properties with their types inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:
// Import TypeScript utilities for type checking here

// Define the ApiResponse interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named 'ApiResponse' is created with the correct property types.
successCriteria: The interface 'ApiResponse' is defined with 'data: string' and 'timestamp: number' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that both properties have the correct types: 'data' should be string and 'timestamp' should be number.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and define both properties with their types.

steps.title: Create a basic type guard function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'isApiResponse' that takes a parameter 'data' of type 'unknown' and returns a boolean.
steps.hint: Start with 'function isApiResponse(data: unknown): boolean { }' or use an arrow function. The function should return true or false.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'isApiResponse' is defined with the correct parameter type and return type.
successCriteria: The function 'isApiResponse' exists, takes a parameter 'data' of type 'unknown', and returns a boolean type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function takes a parameter of type 'unknown' and returns a boolean.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or has incorrect parameters or return type. Check the instruction again.

steps.title: Add type predicate to the type guard
steps.instruction: Modify your existing type guard function to include a type predicate return type that narrows the input to ApiResponse.
steps.hint: Add ': input is ApiResponse' after the parameter list and before the function body's return type annotation.
steps.expectedOutcome: The type guard function now returns a boolean type predicate that tells TypeScript the input is an ApiResponse when true.
successCriteria: The type guard function has a return type annotation with 'input is ApiResponse'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the return type includes 'input is ApiResponse' after the parameter list.
steps.feedbackWrong: The type guard function should have a type predicate return type that narrows to ApiResponse.

steps.title: Implement property existence checks
steps.instruction: Inside your type guard function, add a check to verify that the 'data' property exists in the unknown object.
steps.hint: Use the 'in' operator to test if 'data' is a property of the object.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your type guard function should now check if the 'data' property exists in the object before returning false.
successCriteria: The type guard function includes a check using the 'in' operator to verify the 'data' property exists in the unknown object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the 'in' operator to check if 'data' is a property of the object. The check should return true if the property exists.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on checking property existence. Use the 'in' operator to test if 'data' is a property of the unknown object. Remember to keep the function structure intact.

steps.title: Add type checking for property values
steps.instruction: Inside the isApiResponse function, add type checks to verify that the 'id' property is a number and the 'message' property is a string.
steps.hint: Use the typeof operator to check the type of each property value after confirming the property exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: The type guard now validates both property existence and correct types for id (number) and message (string).
successCriteria: The isApiResponse function includes typeof checks for 'id' and 'message' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some type checks, but make sure to check both 'id' (should be number) and 'message' (should be string).
steps.feedbackWrong: The type guard still needs proper type checking. Use typeof to verify id is a number and message is a string.

steps.title: Create a function to process API responses
steps.instruction: Create a function named processApiResponse that takes an unknown parameter and uses the isApiResponse type guard to safely process the data.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts unknown data, checks it with your type guard, and returns a processed result or error message.
steps.expectedOutcome: A processApiResponse function that uses the type guard to handle unknown API data safely.
successCriteria: The processApiResponse function is defined, accepts unknown parameter, uses isApiResponse type guard, and returns appropriate result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it uses the isApiResponse type guard and handles both valid and invalid cases.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't properly use the type guard. Review how to apply type guards to process unknown data.

steps.title: Add error handling for invalid data
steps.instruction: Inside your processApiResponse function, add an else block that throws an Error when the type guard returns false.
steps.hint: After your if (isApiResponse(data)) block, add else { throw new Error('Invalid API response'); }
steps.expectedOutcome: The processApiResponse function will now throw an error when the type guard fails, providing safe error handling for invalid data.
successCriteria: The processApiResponse function contains an else block that throws an Error when isApiResponse returns false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're throwing an Error object with a descriptive message in the else block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling isn't quite right. Remember to add an else block after the if statement that throws an Error when the type guard fails.

steps.title: Test the type guard with valid data
steps.instruction: Create a test case with valid data to ensure the type guard works correctly. Define a validApiResponse object that matches the ApiResponse interface.
steps.hint: Create an object with the required properties: id (number), name (string), and active (boolean).
steps.expectedOutcome: A validApiResponse object is created with the correct shape to test the type guard.
successCriteria: The validApiResponse object has id (number), name (string), and active (boolean) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a test object, but check that all properties (id, name, active) have the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test object doesn't match the expected structure. Review the ApiResponse interface requirements.

steps.title: Test the type guard with invalid data
steps.instruction: Create a test case with invalid data to verify the type guard properly rejects malformed data.
steps.hint: Call the processApiResponse function with data that does not match the ApiResponse interface, such as an object missing required properties.
steps.analogousExample:
// Testing with invalid data
processApiResponse({ id: 123 }); // Missing 'name' and 'status' properties
steps.expectedOutcome: The type guard should correctly identify invalid data and trigger the error handling path.
successCriteria: A test case with invalid data is added to verify the type guard's error handling.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a test case, but make sure it uses data that doesn't match the ApiResponse interface to fully test the error handling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case doesn't properly test invalid data. Try calling processApiResponse with an object missing required properties like 'name' or 'status'.
